_comment: REFERENCE COPY, and a hand-editable fallback -- not the file to copy blindly. The real .mcp.json is GENERATED by New-McpConfigObject in setup/_common.ps1, which both writers now use: New-Plugin.ps1 writes one into every scaffold, and setup/36-ghidra-mcp.ps1 -WriteMcpConfigTo <dir> writes one into a project that already exists. Generated beats copied because the ghidra command below is the DEFAULT install path and nothing more: setup/30-ghidra.ps1 -GhidraMcpDir can put the bridge anywhere, and it records the real location as bridgeExe in setup/.ghidra-mcp-build.json -- the only thing on the machine that knows it, and what the generator reads. A copy of this file on a machine set up outside C:/repos names an executable that does not exist, so its ghidra server never spawns and the session simply has no Ghidra tools. If you do copy it by hand, fix that command to your own bridge-mcp-ghidra.exe first, and keep the x64dbg pin in step with $script:X64dbgMcpServerPin in setup/_common.ps1, which is where that version now lives. GHIDRA_MCP_URL is REQUIRED for the headless server: bridge discovery probes /mcp/instance_info, which only the Ghidra GUI plugin serves, so without this pin list_instances() finds nothing and no tools register. Drop it only if you are using the GUI; change the port only if you started the server on another one, because it describes a server rather than requesting one.
